messages:
Maya (customer): Hey team — hit a production build break after upgrading @redwood-inference/sdk from 1.3.2 -> 1.4.0. Dev server works, but Vercel production build fails with a bundler error. Anyone seen this?
Tom (eng-runtime): Can you paste the prod build error and your package.json? dev/prod differences often matter.
Maya (customer): Error during the Next.js serverless build: ```Error: Cannot find module '@redwood-inference/sdk' or its corresponding ESM export (ReferenceError: exports is not defined) at Object../node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js```
Maya (customer): package.json minimal: ```{
  "name": "webapp",
  "dependencies": {
    "next": "13.4.6",
    "react": "18.2.0",
    "@redwood-inference/sdk": "^1.4.0"
  },
  "type": "module"
}```
Priya (devex): Thanks — quick guess: 1.4.0 changed the package exports map and added an ESM-only entry that some bundlers choke on when app is `type: \"module\"` + Next's build transforms. Do you see a different error when running `next build` locally with NODE_ENV=production`?
Maya (customer): Local production build reproduces it. We use Vercel (Next on Edge). Error shows up during esbuild step with: ```ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package '.../node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk' imported from /workspace/.next/server/app/_middleware.js```
Tom (eng-runtime): Can you share the top of your lockfile or yarn.lock entry for the sdk? Also, is anything bundling `node_modules` into edge runtime?
Maya (customer): Lockfile shows 1.4.0 with package.json `exports` like: ```"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }```
Jorge (sre): Also seeing a spike in 401s around the same deploy? AlertBot: "Auth service: 401 rate 0.8% -> 12% during 2026-03-14T14:02Z"
Maya (customer): Not related to auth, just build break. We also get tsc warning: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood-inference/sdk'" even though types used to be present in 1.3.x.
Priya (devex): Ok a few things to try while I pull the package: 1) As a workaround, pin back to 1.3.2 to unblock prod. 2) Add an explicit import to cjs entry in webpack/next config: ````webpack(config){ config.resolve.alias['@redwood-inference/sdk'] = require.resolve('@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/cjs/index.js'); return config }```` 3) For Vite/esbuild you can force commonjs with `optimizeDeps.include` or `esbuild` plugin.
Tom (eng-runtime): I'm seeing from the publish logs that 1.4.0 inadvertently omitted the distributed `.d.ts` in the `files` list for the package. That explains the missing types. The exports map should be okay, but Next's edge builds sometimes attempt to load the `import` entry and then fail because of eval transformation. Workaround: import the cjs bundle directly in your edge function: `const Redwood = await import('@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/cjs/index.js')` or `const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/cjs/index.js')` in server runtime.
Maya (customer): Can we avoid modifying code? We prefer a config-only fix.
Tom (eng-runtime): For config-only: set Next.js `experimental.esmExternals = false` or `esbuild` to preserveCommonJS (Next 13 has `experimental: { esmExternals: 'loose' }`). Also adding a webpack alias is config-only.
Maya (customer): Tried `experimental.esmExternals = 'loose'` — still fails but different stack: ```TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'createClient') at Object../node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js``` so it partially loads and then chokes.
Priya (devex): That points to a dual-run scenario where the module namespace isn't initialized correctly after transpile. Quick policy: pin to 1.3.2 and we'll cut 1.4.1 patch that restores CJS-first export and re-adds types.
Tom (eng-runtime): Logged an internal issue ENG-RUNTIME-459 to revert the publish mistake. In the meantime, I'm going to push a small patch build (1.4.1) with: - include dist/index.d.ts - tweak exports so legacy bundlers prefer `require` when `type:module` apps build.
Jorge (sre): From SRE perspective, confirm there are no production runtime regressions for requests that already made it past build. Also check client retries: if someone bundles a mismatched sdk, they may hit auth retries leading to post-deploy 401 noise.
Maya (customer): Fine to pin. Which exact semver to lock to?
Priya (devex): Lock to `@redwood-inference/sdk@1.3.2` in package.json: ```"@redwood-inference/sdk": "1.3.2"``` and delete node_modules + reinstall. That will restore build.
Tom (eng-runtime): ETA for 1.4.1 patch: 3 hours. We'll post changelog and an explicit migration note for Next.js + Edge in the SDK README.
Maya (customer): Thanks — pinning fixed our build. Please ping when 1.4.1 is out so we can test types too. :thumbsup:
AlertBot: "Release draft /packages/sdk v1.4.1 created by @tom — awaiting QA"
Tom (eng-runtime): Filed a follow-up to add a small test matrix for bundler integration (Next Edge, Vite SSR, Webpack serverless) so we catch this in CI.
Maya (customer): Appreciated. Leaving this thread open until confirm types are present.
Priya (devex): I'll follow up with a public workaround doc snippet for our docs site and update support KB. For now: pin, or add webpack alias to cjs, or direct import to dist/cjs as last resort.
